stem: 下列何者最能區分「監督式學習」與「非監督式學習」？

options.label: A
options.text: 監督式學習使用有標籤資料，非監督式學習使用無標籤資料
options.feedback: ✓ 有無標籤是最核心差異

options.label: B
options.text: 監督式學習只能做分類，非監督式只能做回歸
options.feedback: ✗ 兩者都不限於單一任務

options.label: D
options.text: 非監督式學習一定需要 GPU

explanation: 監督式學習的核心特徵是使用有標籤資料（每筆資料都有正確答案），模型從中學習輸入到輸出的映射。非監督式學習使用無標籤資料，模型自行發現資料中的結構與模式。這是兩者最根本的區別。
whyOthersWrong: 監督式學習可做分類也可做迴歸，非監督式學習做聚類而非迴歸。兩者有明確區別，且是否需要 GPU 取決於模型和資料規模，與學習類型無直接關係。

stem: 下列何者屬於非監督式學習常見應用？

options.label: B
options.feedback: ✓ 聚類未標籤資料=非監督式經典應用

explanation: 非監督式學習（Unsupervised Learning）用於處理未標籤資料，常見應用包括聚類（Clustering）、降維和異常偵測。聚類未標籤的客戶行為資料，將客戶分群以發現行為模式，是典型的非監督式學習應用。
whyOthersWrong: 分類已知標籤資料（A）和回歸預測（D）都需要標籤資料，屬於監督式學習。強化學習（C）是第三種學習範式，通過獎勵信號學習，不歸類為非監督式。只有聚類未標籤資料（B）才是非監督式學習。

optionAnalysis.A: 錯誤，因為分類已知標籤資料屬於監督式學習（Supervised Learning），不是非監督式。

stem: Which of the following is a common application of unsupervised learning?
hint: This is a fundamental ML concept question
explanation: Unsupervised learning works with unlabeled data to discover hidden patterns and structures. Clustering—grouping similar data points together—is its most common application. Examples include customer segmentation, anomaly detection, and topic modeling. Supervised learning (classification, regression) requires labeled data, while reinforcement learning uses reward signals.
whyOthersWrong: Classifying labeled data (A) is supervised learning. Reinforcement learning (C) is a third paradigm where agents learn through trial-and-error with reward signals. Supervised regression (D) predicts continuous values from labeled training data.
trap: "Classifying labeled data" is a distractor; choose "Clustering unlabeled behavior"

references.title: What’s the Difference Between Supervised and Unsupervised Learning?
Content Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

optionAnalysis.A: Wrong, because classifying labeled data is supervised learning by definition.
optionAnalysis.B: Correct, because clustering unlabeled data is the textbook example of unsupervised learning.
optionAnalysis.C: Wrong, because reinforcement learning is a separate paradigm using rewards, not unsupervised.
optionAnalysis.D: Wrong, because supervised regression requires labeled data with continuous target values.

plainExplanation: Unsupervised learning is like sorting a mixed bag of coins by size and color without anyone telling you the categories—the algorithm discovers the groups on its own.

stem: A company has 100 labeled customer support tickets and 50,000 unlabeled ones. Which learning approach can leverage BOTH?

options.label: A
options.feedback: supervised learning uses only labeled data, …

options.label: C
options.feedback: semi-supervised learning combines a small am…

options.label: D
options.feedback: rule-based doesn't leverage either data type…

hint: What if you could use a small number of labeled examples plus a large number of unlabeled ones?
explanation: Semi-supervised learning combines a small amount of labeled data with a large amount of unlabeled data. It typically learns the underlying data structure from unlabeled data and uses labeled examples to guide classification. This is practical when labeling is expensive but unlabeled data is abundant.
whyOthersWrong: A) Supervised learning uses only labeled data, ignoring the 50,000 unlabeled examples. B) Unsupervised ignores the 100 valuable labeled examples. D) Rule-based doesn't leverage either data type through learning.
trap: Discarding unlabeled data because it "has no labels" — semi-supervised methods extract value from the underlying patterns in unlabeled data.
mnemonic: Semi-supervised = the best of both worlds. Few labels + many unlabeled = efficient learning.
plainExplanation: Semi-supervised = the best of both worlds. Few labels + many unlabeled = efficient learning.

optionAnalysis.A: Wrong, because supervised learning uses only labeled data, ignoring the 50,000 unlabeled examples.
optionAnalysis.B: Wrong, because unsupervised ignores the 100 valuable labeled examples.
optionAnalysis.D: Wrong, because rule-based doesn't leverage either data type through learning.
optionAnalysis.C: Correct, because semi-supervised learning combines a small amount of labeled data with a large amount of unlabeled data.

stem: What is the typical characteristic of overfitting?

options.label: A
options.text: Good performance on training set, poor on test set

options.label: B
options.text: Poor on both training and test

options.label: C
options.feedback: ✗ Happens in all ML, not just DL

hint: This is a fundamental ML concept question
explanation: Overfitting occurs when a model learns the training data too well, including its noise and peculiarities, resulting in excellent training performance but poor generalization to new, unseen data. It's characterized by a large gap between training accuracy (high) and test/validation accuracy (low).
whyOthersWrong: Poor performance on both sets (B) describes underfitting. Overfitting occurs in all ML algorithms from linear regression to neural networks, not just deep learning (C). Multiple techniques like regularization, cross-validation, and early stopping help prevent overfitting (D).
trap: "Poor on both" is a distractor; choose "good on training, poor on test"
mnemonic: Fundamentals: Overfitting = good train, poor test

references.title: Content Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

optionAnalysis.A: Correct, because overfitting means high training performance but poor generalization to test data.
optionAnalysis.B: Wrong, because poor performance on both training and test is underfitting, not overfitting.
optionAnalysis.C: Wrong, because overfitting can happen in any ML model, not just deep learning.
optionAnalysis.D: Wrong, because regularization, dropout, and early stopping can mitigate overfitting.

plainExplanation: Overfitting is like memorizing a textbook word-for-word but failing the exam because the questions are worded differently. The model 'memorizes' training examples instead of learning general patterns.
